summary:
Phase 0 baseline renderer is done. I wrote M/blender/scripts/tools/render_framings.py, which works in two modes. Inside Blender it renders framings and never saves the .blend. In desktop Python it builds a labelled PIL contact sheet. All 9 framings were rendered from snapshots/museum_stage0_v1.blend at 1280x720, EEVEE, 64 samples, with AgX left as it is in the file. The images are M/blender/renders/baseline/baseline_<name>.png, with a 3x3 labelled sheet at M/blender/renders/baseline/_contact_sheet.jpg. Rendering took 263 s total, 22-42 s per frame. I checked every image by eye, measured luminance, and rendered 5 alternative framings in 2 extra rounds. Those are in renders/baseline/_suggested/ with their own contact sheet. framings.json was NOT edited.

V1 "BEFORE" REFERENCE, per framing (Y = mean / p95 sRGB luminance):
1 rotunda_wide (Y .60/.87): bare white 16-sided plaster drum with a flat 16-sided ceiling at 7 m, lit brightly by the stray 1000 W point light 'Light' at (4.08,1.0,5.9). Plain brown glossy parquet. The east door is a plain rectangular opening with a slightly bent top edge, because the 3.6 m door spans two wall facets. Spine 1 and the Gallery A door are visible through it. The v1 baseboard and picture rail are invisible (hidden inside the wall). No trim, dome, oculus or chandelier.
2 rotunda_dome (Y .64/.91): shows only the flat grey underside of GEO-rotunda_dome_ring1, a solid 16-sided disc at z 7.0-7.3, with a hot spot from 'Light'. Oculus, rings 2-3 and the dome are completely hidden from inside. This is the weakest v1 view.
3 through_door (Y .61/.87): white drum wall framing the east door, with the long grey Spine 1 beyond: two blown-out ceiling light ellipses, gilt baseboard and rail lines, and a dark opening to the stair hall at the far end. Floor warm brown.
4 spine1_west (Y .41/.52): flat grey corridor, dim ambient look. The Gallery A doorway (thin gilt frame, two paintings seen through it) sits in the left third. The right ~40% is a featureless south wall only 0.6 m from the camera. No windows in v1. A faint diagonal seam shows on the ceiling (overlap artefact, see below).
5 gallery_a_north (Y .37/.48): well aimed. About 15 unframed canvases in one row at eye level on a grey-white wall, a thin gilt rail at 6.3 m, flat grey ceiling with a soft glow. The floor fills the lower 30%. Flat, grey, no sense of daylight.
6 gallery_a_corner (Y .39/.65, 1.6% clipped): north and east walls with their painting rows, and a blown-out area-light disc on the ceiling. The upper-right ceiling shows a darker brownish diagonal zone (overlap artefact).
7 gallery_a_art (Y .32/.42): close-up of four paintings (Khusrau miniatures and Giotto), dim and grey, no frames, no picture lights. Paintings nearly touch the bottom edge (about 0.06 m margin).
8 stairs, Phase 3 (Y .40/.42, colour spread .009, essentially monochrome): one long grey block stair, no stringer or balusters, rising left to right against a grey wall; hazy and flat.
9 gallery_f, Phase 3 (Y .40/.65): wide upper gallery with 70 tiny paintings in one row and a blown-out ceiling light. The floor's right half shows off-white plaster instead of parquet (overlap artefact).
Overall v1: every slice view is flat, grey and lit only by the world colour, with blown-out area-light discs, no shadows or bounce light that read as daylight, and little colour (spread .02-.06).

FRAMING SUGGESTIONS (verified by rendering; not applied):
- rotunda_wide: the camera is 0.26 m from the v1 wall face (0.39 m from a 6.6 m-radius v2 shell), so v2 wainscot or pilasters could clip it. Suggest pos [-4.7,-2.9,1.7], target [6.6,0.0,2.9], lens 18 (render alt_rotunda_wide_alt.png; better composed, door centred).
- spine1_west: 0.6 m from the south wall face. Suggest pos [8.6,-1.6,1.7], target [28.0,2.4,2.5], lens 20 (alt_spine1_west_alt3.png): 1.2 m clearance, Gallery A doorway still in the left third, south wall (future windows) at a readable angle.
- gallery_a_art: little room for frame edges and picture lights. Suggest pos [20.0,13.2,1.7], target [20.0,17.0,1.95], lens 28 (alt_gallery_a_art_alt.png): the view covers z of about 0.62-3.2 m on the art wall; the tallest art spans 0.83-2.57.
- Keep the other six. rotunda_dome is correctly aimed for a v2 dome; v1 simply has no visible dome.
api:
CLI (Blender, headless):
  "C:\Program Files\Blender Foundation\Blender 5.2\blender.exe" -b <file.blend> --python-exit-code 1 --python M/blender/scripts/tools/render_framings.py -- --framings all|n1,n2 --out <dir> [--res W H (default 1280 720)] [--samples N (64)] [--engine BLENDER_EEVEE|CYCLES (aliases EEVEE, BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT)] [--prefix str] [--framings-file path (default M/blender/scripts/framings.json)] [--fov-source lens|fov (default lens)] [--percent 100] [--device CPU|GPU (Cycles only, default CPU)] [--skip-existing] [--dry-run] [--list]
  Output: <out>/<prefix><name>.png, 8-bit RGB PNG. Prints 'RENDERED <name> <path> <secs>' per frame and a final 'RENDER_FRAMINGS_DONE {"n":..,"failed":[..],"seconds":..,"files":[..]}'. Exit code 1 on any failure or unknown framing name, 2 if --out is missing.
Python API (inside Blender; sys.path.insert(0, r"...\blender\scripts\tools"); import render_framings as RF):
  RF.load_framings(path=None) -> (framings_dict, meta_dict)
  RF.select_framings(framings, spec) -> [names]  (spec 'all' | 'a,b' | list; KeyError on unknown names)
  RF.look_at_matrix(pos, target, up=(0,0,1)) -> 4x4 mathutils.Matrix (camera looks down -Z, no roll, handles straight up/down)
  RF.place_camera(cam_obj, framing, fov_source='lens', clip=(0.05,1000)) -> {lens, sensor_fit, hfov, loc}
  RF.render_framings(names=None|'all'|list, out_dir, res=(1280,720), samples=64, engine='BLENDER_EEVEE', prefix='', framings_file=None, fov_source='lens', percent=100, device=None, skip_existing=False, dry_run=False, scene=None) -> [ {name, path, status 'ok'|'skipped'|'dry_run'|'missing_output', seconds, lens, hfov, ...} ]
    It never saves. It snapshots and restores scene.camera, engine, resolution, %, filepath, image format, EEVEE/Cycles samples, Cycles device and view settings, and deletes the temporary camera '_TMP-render_framings_cam' in a finally block. Colour management is never changed.
  RF.lens_to_vfov_deg(lens_mm, aspect=16/9) -> vertical fov (three.js) for a 36 mm horizontal-fit sensor.
Desktop Python (PIL): <_RAG/.venv/Scripts/python.exe> render_framings.py --contact-sheet <dir> [--pattern "baseline_*.png"] [--sheet-out path (default <dir>/_contact_sheet.jpg)] [--cols 3] [--thumb 640] [--title str] [--order n1,n2,..]. Labels come from framings.json (name, lens, slice/phase 3, desc). The text of the pattern before '*' is stripped from each file name to get the framing name. Files starting with '_' are skipped. Callable as RF.contact_sheet(src_dir, pattern, out_path, cols, thumb_w, title, order, framings_file).
tests:
1) Low-res test (480x270, 16 samples, 2 framings), images checked: camera aim correct. 2) Full baseline: 9/9 rendered, exit 0, 263.5 s total (rotunda_wide 41.9 s including shader compile, others 21.6-33.7 s), all 9 PNGs checked. Luminance stats per image were computed with PIL/numpy (listed in the summary). 3) Contact-sheet mode tested on the test images and on the baseline (1960x1308 JPG, 9 labelled tiles); checked visually. 4) Alternative framings: 2 extra rounds (5 variants, 960x540, 32 samples) using --framings-file with a scratch JSON; all checked. 5) API self-test inside Blender (scratch test_rf.py):
   - look_at_matrix passes for all 9 framings (forward matches the direction to the target within 1e-5, camera X axis horizontal so no roll, camera up has +Z) and for a straight-up view.
   - dry_run works for all.
   - fov_source='fov' gives an equivalent lens of 13.51 mm and a 106.2 deg horizontal fov for gallery_a_north, confirming the fov_deg mismatch.
   - An unknown name raises KeyError.
   - A tiny Cycles CPU render (160x90, 2 samples) succeeds.
   - Scene state is identical before and after (camera 'Camera', EEVEE, 1280x960, filepath, RGBA PNG, 64/4096 samples, AgX, 484 objects, 2 cameras) and the temp camera is removed.
   - bpy.data.is_dirty is True, as expected (memory only, nothing saved).
6) py_compile OK with desktop Python.
known_issues: framings.json fov_deg values are wrong for 16:9. They equal the vertical FOV of a 36x27 mm (4:3) frame, 2*atan(13.5/lens), and 16 and 20 mm are also slightly off (79.6 vs 80.3, 67.4 vs 68.0). The correct three.js vertical fov at 16:9 for lens_mm on a 36 mm horizontal sensor is 2*atan(10.125/lens): 16mm=64.7, 18mm=58.7, 20mm=53.7, 24mm=45.7, 28mm=39.8. Using fov_deg as it stands in the web ?view= makes browser screenshots much wider than the Blender renders (18mm: 106 deg vs 90 deg horizontal). The file may have been derived from the blend's own 1280x960 (4:3) render resolution. Web/debug.js should compute the fov from lens_mm or use corrected values. render_framings uses lens_mm by default; --fov-source fov reproduces the web fov.

v1 geometry has coplanar overlapping slabs that z-fight in renders. GEO-gallery_f_floor, spanning x 8..28, y -10..10, z 6.9..7.1, has the same z range as GEO-gallery_a_ceiling (x 12..28, y 3..17) and GEO-spine1_ceiling (x 7..84, y -3..3). GEO-spine2_floor (x 28..84) also coincides with spine1_ceiling. Visible as the plaster-coloured right half of the floor in baseline_gallery_f, the brownish diagonal zone on the ceiling in baseline_gallery_a_corner, and the faint ceiling seam in the spine1 renders. v2 ceilings/laylights for gallery_a and spine1 must sit below z 6.9, or the v1 ceilings must be retired. Otherwise the gallery_f framing will keep flickering.

The v1 rotunda ceiling is GEO-rotunda_dome_ring1, a solid 16-sided disc of radius 6.6 at z 7.0-7.3. It hides the oculus and upper rings from inside, so baseline_rotunda_dome shows only a flat grey slab. A stray 1000 W point light named 'Light' at (4.08,1.0,5.9), likely Blender's default light, makes the hot spot in the rotunda renders. Integration may want to delete or retire it for v2 (not my file).
The snapshot's scene render settings are 1280x960 (4:3) and scene.camera is 'Camera'. render_framings sets 1280x720 per run and restores the originals.

Many other Blender processes were running at the same time. One alternative render reported 21791 s because the machine apparently slept between 02:29 and 08:31 (the file was written at 02:29). Per-frame timings are wall-clock and unreliable if the host sleeps.
Blender's stdout is block-buffered when redirected to a file, so progress lines show up in bursts; use the output files and the final RENDER_FRAMINGS_DONE line as the source of truth.
Cycles defaults to CPU. --device GPU tries OPTIX, CUDA, HIP, ONEAPI and METAL in turn and falls back to CPU; this was not tested on GPU here.
integration_notes:
Reuse for v2 before/after renders:
  blender -b M/blender/museum.blend --python-exit-code 1 --python M/blender/scripts/tools/render_framings.py -- --framings all --out M/blender/renders/v2 --res 1280 720 --samples 64 --prefix v2_
then build the sheet with:
  M/../_RAG/.venv/Scripts/python.exe M/blender/scripts/tools/render_framings.py --contact-sheet M/blender/renders/v2 --pattern "v2_*.png" --title "v2"
For quick dev checks use --res 960 540 --samples 32. Blender load is about 20-90 s and the first frame includes about 20 s of shader compile.
museum_lib_v2.render_framing() can wrap it with RF.render_framings([name], out_dir, res, samples, engine, prefix=...), since the module is importable and restores all state. It still marks the blend dirty in memory, so do not call it right before save_stage unless that is intended; the temp camera is always removed.
Keep baseline_<name>.png as the 'before' images. They are the same size (1280x720) and colour pipeline (AgX, exposure 0, look None) for side-by-side comparison.
If the orchestrator adopts the suggested framings, it (the owner of framings.json) should update rotunda_wide, spine1_west and gallery_a_art and correct fov_deg as noted, and baselines for those three should then be re-rendered with: --framings rotunda_wide,spine1_west,gallery_a_art --out M/blender/renders/baseline --prefix baseline_ (then re-run the contact sheet).
Files in renders/baseline/_suggested/ are illustrative only.
